body.p: In response to the Final Office Action mailed June 13, 2024, claims 2 and 12 have been canceled without prejudice, and claims 1, 3, 11, 13, and 18 have been amended. No new matter has been introduced. Accordingly, claims 1, 3-11, and 13-20 are currently pending.

In the Final Office Action, the drawings were objected to. In addition, claims 1 and 5-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by International Publication No. WO 2000/ 029287 ("Syta"). Finally, claim 11 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over Syta reference in view of U.S. Patent No. 3,714,987 ("Mattson"), claims 2-4, 12-14, 18, and 19 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 103 as unpatentable over Syta in view of Mattson and U.S. Publication No. 2012/ 0018569 ("Toni"), claims 11 and 15-17 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 103 as unpatentable over Syta in view of Mattson and U.S. Patent No. 2,973,923 ("the Sznycer"), and claims 11 and 20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 103 as unpatentable over Syta in view of Mattson and "the Rugged and Economic H215 Ready for the U.S. Market" ("Airbus NPL"). Because none of the cited references, either alone or in combination, disclose, teach, or suggest the subject matter of the present claims, the rejections should be withdrawn.

Applicant appreciates the Examiner's indication that claim 19 would be allowable if rewritten in independent form. Applicant will address claim 19 when the final status of the application is determined.
In response to the Final Office Action, Claim 1 has been amended to recite "an

attachment mechanism comprising: a linking assembly having a head connector, a tail connector attached to the upper frame structure, and an adjustment mechanism disposed between the head connector and the tail connector, the adjustment mechanism being rotatably manipulable to

adjust the distance between the head connector and the tail connector; and a rod pivotably attached to the head connector of the linking assembly and extending upwardly therefrom to an upper end portion, the upper end portion of the rod being configured to attach to a main rotor transmission of the helicopter to suspend therefrom." Similarly, claim 11 has been amended to recite "a tank assembly comprising...an attachment mechanism comprising: a linking assembly having a head connector, a tail connector attached to the upper frame structure, and an adjustment mechanism disposed between the head connector and the tail connector, the adjustment mechanism being rotatably manipulable to adjust the distance between the head connector and the tail connector; and a rod pivotably attached to the head connector of the linking assembly and extending upwardly therefrom to an upper end portion, the upper end portion of the rod being attached to the main rotor transmission to suspend therefrom." Support for these amendments can be found in at least para. [0056] and Figs. 4 and 10. Objection to the Drawings

With respect to the objections to the drawings, submitted herewith are replacement sheets replacing original FIGS. 5 and 19-21. No new matter has been introduced. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1)
Claims 1 and 5-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by the WO 2000/029287 ("Syta"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.

Applicant respectfully submits that Syta fails to disclose or suggest at least "A tank assembly for a helicopter, the tank assembly comprising... an attachment mechanism comprising: a linking assembly having a head connector, a tail connector attached to the upper frame structure, and an adjustment mechanism disposed between the head connector and the tail connector, the adjustment mechanism being rotatably manipulable to adjust the distance

between the head connector and the tail connector; and a rod pivotably attached to the head connector of the linking assembly and extending upwardly therefrom to an upper end portion, the upper end portion of the rod being configured to attach to a main rotor transmission of the helicopter to suspend therefrom" as recited in claim 1 of the present application (emphasis added).
On page 5 of the Final Office Action, the Examiner asserts that the supports 1 and/or

connecting pieces 2 are equivalent to the presently claimed attachment mechanism. However, the supports 1 and/or connecting pieces 2 of Syta clearly do not include a linking assembly and a rod as recited in proposed amended claim 1 of the present application.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Syta fails to disclose or suggest each and every feature of claim 1 of the present application.
Applicant also respectfully submits that dependent claims 5-10 are not anticipated by Syta at least by virtue of their dependencies on claim 1. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103

Claim 11 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Syta and US 3,714,987 ("Mattson"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. Applicant respectfully submits that Syta fails to disclose or suggest at least "a tank assembly comprising...an attachment mechanism comprising: a linking assembly having a head connector, a tail connector attached to the upper frame structure, and an adjustment mechanism disposed between the head connector and the tail connector, the adjustment mechanism being rotatably manipulable to adjust the distance between the head connector and the tail connector; and a rod pivotably attached to the head connector of the linking assembly and extending upwardly therefrom to an upper end portion, the upper end portion of the rod being attached to the main rotor
transmission to suspend therefrom," as recited in claim 11 of the present application, for similar reasons discussed above for claim 1.
Mattson fails to remedy these deficiencies. Mattson discloses a helicopter with a fire

suppression system including a water tank 32 with a cargo hook engaging swivel 44 that engages the cargo hook 42 of the helicopter 20. However, there does not appear to be any disclosure in Mattson of the cargo hook engaging swivel 44 being rotatably manipulable so as to adjust its length/height.

Accordingly, there is simply no motivation, nor would it have been obvious, for one of ordinary skill in the art to manipulate the arrangements of Syta and Mattson against their specific teachings in order to arrive at the invention defined in claim 11 of the present application. Applicant also submits that even if one of ordinary skill in the art could be reasonably expected to combine the disclosures of Syta and Mattson (which the Applicant denies), such a combination would still not arrive at the invention defined in claim 11 of the present application.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 11 is patentable in view of Syta and Mattson.
Claims 2-4 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Syta, Mattson and US 2012/018569 ("Toni"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claims 2-4 directly or indirectly depend from claim 1, and/or include all of the

limitations of claim 1. As discussed above, Syta fails to teach or suggest at least "an attachment mechanism comprising: a linking assembly having a head connector, a tail connector attached to the upper frame structure, and an adjustment mechanism disposed between the head connector and the tail connector, the adjustment mechanism being rotatably manipulable to adjust the distance between the head connector and the tail connector; and a rod pivotably attached to the

head connector of the linking assembly and extending upwardly therefrom to an upper end portion, the upper end portion of the rod being configured to attach to a main rotor transmission of the helicopter to suspend therefrom," as recited in claim 1 of the present application. Mattson and Toni fail to remedy these deficiencies.

Claims 12-14 and 18 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Syta, Mattson and Toni. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. Claims 12-14 and 18 directly or indirectly depend from claim 11, and/or include all of the limitations of claim 11. As discussed above, Syta fails to teach or suggest at least "a tank assembly comprising...an attachment mechanism comprising: a linking assembly having a head connector, a tail connector attached to the upper frame structure, and an adjustment mechanism disposed between the head connector and the tail connector, the adjustment mechanism being rotatably manipulable to adjust the distance between the head connector and the tail connector; and a rod pivotably attached to the head connector of the linking assembly and extending upwardly therefrom to an upper end portion, the upper end portion of the rod being attached to the main rotor transmission to suspend therefrom," as recited in claim 11 of the present application.

Claims 11 and 15-17 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Syta and US 2,973,923 ("Sznycer"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. As discussed above, Syta fails to disclose or suggest at least "a tank assembly comprising...an attachment mechanism comprising: a linking assembly having a head connector, a tail connector attached to the upper frame structure, and an adjustment mechanism disposed between the head connector and the tail connector, the adjustment mechanism being rotatably manipulable to adjust the distance between the head connector and the tail connector; and a rod pivotably attached to the head connector of the linking assembly and extending upwardly therefrom to an upper end

portion, the upper end portion of the rod being attached to the main rotor transmission to suspend therefrom," as recited in claim 11 of the present application. Sznycer fails to remedy these deficiencies.

There is simply no motivation, nor would it have been obvious, for one of ordinary skill in the art to manipulate the arrangements of Syta and Sznycer against their specific teachings in order to arrive at the invention defined in claim 11 of the present application. Applicant also submits that even if one of ordinary skill in the art could be reasonably expected to combine the disclosures of Syta and Sznycer (which the Applicant denies), such a combination would still not arrive at the invention defined in claim 11 of the present application.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 11 is patentable in view of Syta and Sznycer.
Claims 15-17 directly or indirectly depend from claim 11, and/or include all of the
limitations of claim 11. Accordingly, dependent claims 15-17 are also believed to be patentable in view of Syta and Sznycer.

Claims 11 and 20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Syta and NPL entitled "The rugged and economic H215 ready for the U.S. market" ("Airbus NPL"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. As discussed above, Syta fails to disclose or suggest at least "a tank assembly comprising...an attachment mechanism comprising: a linking assembly having a head connector, a tail connector attached to the upper frame structure, and an adjustment mechanism disposed between the head connector and the tail connector, the adjustment mechanism being rotatably manipulable to adjust the distance between the head connector and the tail connector; and a rod pivotably attached to the head connector of the linking assembly and extending upwardly therefrom to an upper end portion, the upper end

portion of the rod being attached to the main rotor transmission to suspend therefrom," as recited in claim 11 of the present application. Applicant submits that Airbus NPL fails to remedy these deficiencies.

There is simply no motivation, nor would it have been obvious, for one of ordinary skill in the art to manipulate the arrangements of Syta and Airbus NPL against their specific teachings in order to arrive at the invention defined in claim 11 of the present application.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 11 is patentable in view of Syta and Airbus NPL.
Claim 20 directly depends from claim 11, and includes all of the limitations of claim 11. Accordingly, dependent claim 20 is also believed to be patentable in view of Syta and Airbus NPL.

In view of the foregoing, it is submitted that the claims now presented in this application define patentable subject matter over the cited prior art. Accordingly, reconsideration and allowance of the application is requested.
